g.text: Historian Foster Rhea Dulles claims US foreign policy was isolationist in 1920sHistorian Arthur Schelsinger Jr states in 1920s US retreated into ‘soothing isolationism’George C Herring argues that involvement without commitment seems the bast way to sum up the US approach to the world during the period. The nation vigorously promoted its interests while scrupulously guarding against entanglements. Historian Herfried Münkler believes the objective of US entry into the First World War was to become a world power. Treasury Secretary William Gibbs McAdoo had already developed plans to replace British £ with US $ as leading international reserve currency.William A Williams argues isolationism was a myth. Republicans in 1920s were highly involved in affairs of other nationsGeorge C Herring claims there were ‘unprecedented levels of involvement’ in 1920s. US often used ‘soft power’ –influence using economic, cultural and technological superiority rather than military force.
